messages.subject: Peaks detection
parts:
Greetings,

I would like to determine the number of peaks in the frequency of a
wave with respect to time. The closest function I have found is the
fpeaks function, but this function looks for peaks in the frequency
spectrum, not in the frequency of a wave along the time axis. Could
you please give me suggestions as to how this can be accomplished.

Sincerely,
Jonathan

messages.author: e53f91d0708becab
messages.subject: Re: Peaks detection
parts:
Yes, that's basically this and you have much more functionalities
available.

You'll find another 2 parameters on last version of seewave timer():
s.start and s.end. Start and End time (in sec) for each identified
pulse.

I've being playing with seewave. Some notes of mine:
For the ith pulse of bat_lft:

#! Mean frequency spectrum
m_bat[[i]] = if(
length(cutw(bat_lft, from = pos_bat$s.start[i], to = pos_bat
$s.end[i],
out = "Wave")@left) > 512
){meanspec(
cutw(bat_lft, from = pos_bat$s.start[i], to = pos_bat$s.end[i],
out = "Wave"), plot = F, fftw = T)}else meanspec(
cutw(batlft, from = pos_bat$s.start[i], to = pos_bat$s.end[i] +
0.02,
out = "Wave"), plot = F, fftw = T)
#! Peak
peak_bat = fpeaks(m_bat[[i]], nmax = 1, plot = F)[1, 1]*1000 #! hz
#! Parameters set
#! Efficiency use of memory ?? Será pouco eficiente no uso da
memória (data.frame)
#sprop_bat[[i]] = as.data.frame(specprop(m_bat[[i]], plot = F))[ ,
1:12]
#sprop_bat[[i]] = specprop(m_bat[[i]], plot = F) #! to test
sprop_bat[[i]]$peak = peak_bat
#! Initial frequency
sprop_bat[[i]]$f_ini = dfreq(bat_lft, at = pos_bat$s.start[i],
plot = F)[2, 2]*1000
#! Final frequency
sprop_bat[[i]]$f_fim = dfreq(bat_lft, at = c(pos_bat$s.end[i]),
plot = F)[2, 2]*1000
#! Level of entropy
sprop_bat[[i]]$entropy = mean(csh(
cutw(bat_lft, from = pos_bat$s.start[i], to = pos_bat$s.end[i],
out = "Wave"), plot = F)[ ,2])
#sprop_bat[[i]]$esp = esp_list$esp[esp_list$file == list_wav[j]]
sprop_bat[[i]]$file = list_wav[j]

Good luck

Paulo
